claim: Policy content, supported inline structure, and review status have stable Yjs identity separate from Lexical root placement, allowing readiness-gated shared reorder without move-versus-edit loss.
commands: npm --prefix frontend run test -- src/workspace/policyContentModel.test.ts src/workspace/policyContentLexical.test.ts src/workspace/policyContentBridge.test.ts src/workspace/PolicyContentBridgeProvider.ui.test.tsx src/workspace/editorStructure.test.ts src/migrations.test.ts src/workspace/projectModel.test.ts src/workspace/projectArchive.test.ts --reporter=verbose
proved: Each stable policy ID maps to one deterministically named top-level Y.Text carrying schema version, draft/review/approved state, character content, supported text attributes, and bounded serialized inline embeds.
Content updates use character-level Yjs operations and attribute formatting rather than replacing an opaque whole-text value.
The strict Lexical adapter round-trips bold/italic text, style, line breaks, scenario-reference embeds, and policy status, and rejects block embeds before mutation.
Local project migration validates every seed before the first write, initializes all pending records in one Yjs transaction, is idempotent, and rejects conflicts without partial backfill.

The live bridge mirrors genuine local edits into stable records and projects canonical remote records with Yjs writeback skipped, preventing duplicate transport packets and local undo-history pollution.
Two bound editors preserve the edited policy ID, text formatting, and status when a peer moves that block during a partition and both reconnect.
Separate append-only move and edit/status packets converge to the same visible order and content when replayed move-first or edit-first.
Stable policy records survive normal project Yjs replication and the checksummed portable project archive.
Drive reorder is enabled only after the live bridge is healthy with zero legacy policy IDs; checking, invalid, and legacy states show a reason and register no move command.
The obsolete expected-failure fixture is gone; the complete frontend suite has no expected failures.
notProved: Two packaged physical installations reordered and edited the same stable policy block through a real Drive workspace.
Existing Drive-shared legacy policy blocks have a safe automatic multi-peer baseline migration; they remain visibly reorder-closed.
Delete-versus-edit policy semantics, coordinated legacy migration, compaction, or recovery after malicious canonical-record damage.
A 100-page or 500,000-code-unit policy document meets a measured typing, migration, projection, memory, and reconnect latency budget.
Packaged pointer, keyboard, undo/redo, screen-reader, narrow-layout, reduced-motion, and every-theme interaction.
A release/updater artifact contains this development checkpoint.
